paragraphs: Let us put it to them: tell us about your statement "we do not know a thing except when we are compelled to its knowledge"[{2}] — do you know that this statement of yours is itself sound by way of necessity, or by some other route? If they reply that they know it not by way of necessity, they have annulled their own thesis (which was that they know things only by way of necessity); they have thereby acknowledged a knowledge that does not depend on necessity, and they have confirmed the soundness of rational reflection.[{3}] If they reply that they do know it by way of necessity, we then ask them: must we, then, be partners with you in this knowledge — that is, must we likewise be compelled to whatever it is that you are compelled to? If they answer that we must,[{4}] there is no longer any difference between their claim that we are of necessity compelled to acknowledge the soundness of their thesis (namely, that nothing is known except by necessity) and our claim that we are of necessity compelled to acknowledge the unsoundness of their thesis, and that we know — of necessity — that they cannot know anything except by necessity is itself false.[{5}]
So it may be said: this is the kind of internal contradiction (ilzām)[{6}] that attaches to the position they have committed themselves to in the face of those who hold the opposing view. ---
